answers.falsifier: Done when: an AST scan of cairn/devices/web_server/groundloop/pulse.py finds no call to os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname or socket.gethostname, and every host name those files read comes from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name AND with os.uname deleted from the os module for the call, is_cairn_home(host_name().upper() + '.lan', addresses=()) is True and is_cairn_home('testing-web-not-this-box', addresses=()) is False. Wrong intent if the system device's tool cannot answer here (an import cycle, or a caller that must run before cairn is on sys.path).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a child of spanning ticket a577fd03e307, whose measured sites were grepped over cairn/devices/system_rackmount/rackmount.py's neighbours on 2026-11-21 and whose ruling is outline 6.6.3.7 in cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/06-recovery-device.md
answers.how: pulse.py:83's default `platform.node()` becomes a lazy `host_name()` from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host; the explicit `me=` argument stays for callers that pass one. groundloop/ has no charter of its own, so it rides the web_server device's charter and proofs dir.
answers.traces_to: Outline 6.6.3.7 (the hostname comes from the system device); outline 2.3.7.1.5 (the system device's host tool is one of the client tools a device publishes, the named exception to 2.3.7; a CC by-line builds, 0.4.1); outline 17.26.1 (a published client tool lives with its device); RULE 1 (the system device's public interface is the tool it publishes); Law 1 (one answer, not N re-derivations of it).
answers.what: The web server's ground-loop pulse names its host through the system device's host tool: cairn/devices/web_server/groundloop/pulse.py:83 read the host from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host and nowhere else, so this component names its box on every OS.
